title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Holds, Resumption and Administrative Closure
content:
Patient services desk guidance note on holds and administrative closures of a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

## Hold reasons

An active program is placed on hold for exactly one recorded reason, and a hold is placed only for a reason that is true on the date of the write.

| Hold reason | True when | The hold clears when |
|---|---|---|
| Inpatient stay | The customer or caregiver reports a current inpatient admission to a hospital or skilled nursing facility, on tiers where an inpatient hold is required | Discharge is reported |
| Coverage lapse | The coverage record the program bills has a termination date earlier than the date of the write and no other in-effect coverage on file fixes the program's tier | An in-effect coverage on file is written onto the program |
| Documentation lapse | No authorization grant of the program is valid on the date of the write | An authorization grant is valid on the date of the write |
| Past-due balance | See the retired clause below | A past-due amount below the tier's past-due hold minimum, or an approved payment plan |
| Customer request | The customer asks to pause shipments | The customer asks to resume |

A program on hold resumes only when its recorded hold reason has cleared.

**Retired clause: the past-due balance reason.** As originally written for every use, the reason read: past-due balance, on tiers where the past-due age is greater than 0 days, when the past-due amount is at least the tier's past-due hold minimum and no approved payment plan covers it. In that unqualified form it is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, which gives the ship-time past-due test of the refill count for a delivery drawing on the grant resting on the newest written order, and of the plan member waiver count, a test of their own; every program hold for a past-due balance still rests on the reason exactly as just quoted.

**The past-due amount for a hold.** The past-due amount is the greater of 0.00 and the total of the program's remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds posted more than the tier's past-due age in calendar days before the date of the test, less the total of all payments and balance adjustments posted on or before the test date, in USD; payments and credits are applied to the oldest postings first.

## Administrative closure

A program closes administratively, with the matching closure reason, in exactly these cases:

| Closure reason | Case |
|---|---|
| Documentation not received | A program still in referral received or pending authorization once the date of the write is later than the enrolled date plus the tier's referral documentation window, with no prior authorization decision pending |
| Authorization denied | A payer prior authorization denial stands and no new request is pending |
| Hold limit reached | A program on hold once the date of the write is later than the hold start date plus the tier's hold limit |
| Coverage ended | A program on hold for coverage lapse whose customer reports no replacement coverage |
| Customer discontinued | The customer confirms the cancellation of a program on hold |
| Deceased | Larkfield's records team has recorded the customer's death |

Day counts here are calendar days counted from the named date, and a closure is made only on a day strictly later than the named date plus the stated days.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

- **Hold limit.** Suppose a hold limit of 60 days and a hold start date of 1 March of a non-leap year. The named date plus 60 days is 30 April: on 30 April the program cannot yet be closed for the hold limit; on 1 May it can.
- **Referral window.** Suppose a window of 30 days and an enrolled date of 1 June: the named date plus 30 days is 1 July, so closure for documentation not received is possible from 2 July, and only while no prior authorization decision is pending.
- **Past-due amount.** Suppose a past-due age of 90 days, postings of 100.00 USD 120 days ago and 50.00 USD 10 days ago, and payments of 30.00 USD: only the 100.00 USD posting is older than 90 days, so the past-due amount is 100.00 USD less 30.00 USD, that is 70.00 USD.

superseded_clauses: past_due_balance (on tiers where past_due_hold_days is greater than 0, the past-due amount measured by cgm_msr_past_due_amount is at least past_due_hold_min_usd and no approved payment plan covers it)
